slices.name: Baseline, source contract and allocation
acceptance: Clean baseline recorded
Original requirements and injections mapped
Every writer has disjoint ownership

slices.name: Lean core behavior and philosophy
acceptance: Always-loaded core is behavior-first and non-duplicative
Meaningful-question and automatic-execution behavior is explicit
Rules remain concise without deleting verification strength

slices.name: Adaptive plan, orchestration and detailed ledger protocol
acceptance: One shared work protocol owns classification, task packets and terminal behavior
Plan contract scales without losing executability
Ledger rules preserve source/injection mapping and are required only when useful
Model routing uses economy/standard/expert with effort cap high

slices.name: Claim-driven proof and ground-truth benchmark
acceptance: Profiles cover business, distributed consistency, query/index, cache and resource lifetime
Negative fixtures measure false PASS
Benchmark counts main plus sub-agent cost and separates build proof from behavior proof

slices.name: Automatic work state and orchestration automation
acceptance: Automatic small/medium/large/resumable classification
Detailed resumable ledger with source allocation and agent receipts
Atomic state updates and safe concurrent assignment
No user CLI ceremony

slices.name: Native adapters, router cutover, tool registry and legacy cleanup
acceptance: Native capability states are truthful on all four platforms
Cursor uses current native hooks
Graph router cuts over after one measured shadow cycle
Default Stop coercion and production legacy indirection are removed

slices.name: Cross-review, validation, runtime install, commit and push
acceptance: Each slice receives independent risk-based review
Full validator, health audit, router, workctl and benchmark suites pass
Runtime mirrors and native receipts are reported truthfully
Integrated diff is committed and pushed to origin/main
